abstract: A Digital Twin (DT) replicates objects, processes, or systems in real-time within cyberspace for various applications, such as railway defect inspection. Such an application can benefit from DTs when integrated with Artificial Intelligence (AI) by enabling advanced data analysis, predictive maintenance, and other capabilities. Defect inspection can integrate pre-trained Large Language Models (LLMs) into DT ecosystem as its AI component to simulate defects, thereby reducing the reliance on extensive real-world defect data. Mobile-friendly tools that leverage this AI integration can help railway operators identify and understand defects directly from video streams, images, or text. Motivated by this scope, we propose the DefectTwin ecosystem and its mobile application for railway defect inspection. DefectTwin employs a multimodal AI pipeline to analyze both seen and unseen visual defects.

abstract: A finite-element model of the direct-drive coreless permanent-magnet generator is used to simulate faults individually. Each fault case—rotor magnet demagnetization, a stator inter-turn short circuit, static eccentricity, and dynamic eccentricity—is introduced into the finite-element analysis (FEA) model separately, rather than in combination. For each isolated fault scenario, the stator current signals are processed using the Extended Park’s Vector Approach (EPVA) and the electromagnetic torque is examined in the frequency domain. The EPVA spectra and torque harmonics exhibit unique features for each fault type, allowing for clear discrimination among faults. These results demonstrate that modeling and analyzing faults one at a time yields distinct diagnostic signatures. © 2025 by the authors.

A standard solution to it is to incorporate operational parameters into learning framework, but doing so can be costly and often infeasible if such data are not available in practice. abstract: Core burr defects are latent sources of electric field distortion and insulation degradation in oil-immersed power transformers. abstract: The reliability analysis of railway rolling stock systems determines how efficiently passenger services operate and how sustainable operations remain over a specified period.
